title: How can next-token prediction learn math? Start with one trainable parameter
summary:
Next-token prediction is an objective, not a restriction that a model must only count neighboring words. A tiny model makes one part of the distinction visible.
We supply the structure y_hat = w*x and train only w. Examples use x=3 with target 6 and x=5 with target 10. The model does not discover multiplication: multiplication is built in.
With squared loss (w*x-y)^2, the gradient is 2*x*(w*x-y). For this demonstration, a learning rate of 1/(4*x*x) halves the distance from w to 2 at every step.
